sections.title: 🎯 What You'll Learn
sections.content:
Let’s demystify how to call methods in Java! Think of methods as little helpers that do specific tasks for you.

• How to invoke (call) a method
• The role of parentheses and semicolons
• Practical examples with `System.out.println()` and `Scanner`

sections.title: 💡 Concept Explanation
sections.content:
Imagine methods like vending machines. You press a button (call a method), and it gives you what you want—like a soda or a snack!

In Java, calling a method is just as simple:
• You write the method’s name
• Add parentheses `()` (like pressing the button)
• End with a semicolon `;` (like confirming your choice)

For example, `System.out.println("Hello!")` tells Java to print "Hello!" to the console. The `println` method is like the vending machine’s "print" button.

sections.title: 📊 Visual Simulation
sections.content: Step-by-step visualization of how Calling a Method works:

steps.title: Write the Method Name
steps.description: Start with the object (like `System.out`) and the method name (like `println`).

steps.title: Add Parentheses
steps.description: Parentheses `()` hold the input (like a message or number).

steps.title: End with a Semicolon
steps.description: The semicolon `;` tells Java you’re done with the statement.

sections.title: 🔥 Tips & Mistakes
donts: Call methods without their object (e.g., `println()` alone won’t work)
sections.protip: If a method isn’t working, check for typos and missing parentheses first!

sections.title: 🌍 Real World Use
sections.content: Where is Calling a Method used in real apps?

examples.how: Call `calculateInterest()` to compute savings growth or `validatePin()` to check user input.
Call `jump()` or `shoot()` methods when players press buttons.

problem.description: Write a program that asks the user for their name and then prints a greeting. Use `Scanner.nextLine()` to read input and `System.out.println()` to print the message.
hints: Store the name in a variable (e.g., `String name`)
problem.explanation: We called `input.nextLine()` to read the user’s name and `System.out.println()` to print the greeting. Parentheses and semicolons are key!

sections.title: 📝 Summary
points: 📌 Practice with `println()` and `Scanner` to build confidence
📌 Ready to learn about *return values* next!
